_doc: The Spatial & Environmental Blueprint (docs/SPATIAL_BLUEPRINT.md): the master specification every map is built to, and the gate the build checks each map against. Metres; x across, y up, z into the screen from the launcher. The camera sits 3 m behind the launcher.

corridor.why: the throw lane, the ring's space and the boss's patch: scenery never stands in it (behind z 16, decoration may). Only gameplay objects (the ring, its anchor's hanger, targets and obstacles) cross it.

structure.why: v47: every map is 80 hits in 10-hit sections. Acts I–III (1–30), the mini-boss (31–40: ten hits and the ring breaks loose), the approach (41–50), then the end boss in three phases of ten (51–60, 61–70, 71–80). Every ten hits something changes. Boss Rush keeps its short fights.

foreground.rule: gameplay-critical: everything the throw can touch

midground.rule: gameplay and interaction: it reacts to the throw, it never blocks it

background.rule: atmosphere: nothing here competes with the ring (no ring-coloured glow within its screen band)

parallax.why: camera distances are compressed toward the ring's (a multiplane rig), so far planes still move: this is physical depth, not decorative scrolling

base.why: fixed readable framing: the skull rests at 77% down the screen, the ring hangs at 34%

ringSafe.why: no camera move may push the ring out of this box on the screen (fractions of the width and height)

reactions.move: slides or swings away from the hit, then settles
reactions.rotate: turns about its pivot, then turns back
reactions.bend: leans away from the hit and springs back past upright
reactions.crack: a crack is drawn in and stays for the map
reactions.fall: topples over and lies there for the map
reactions.squeak: a short squash and a squeak
reactions.react: a character looks, jumps or shouts

ambientBudget.why: alive but mechanically quiet: at most seven ambient animations a map, two of them big

impact.why: a hit lights the frame for a moment

boss.why: the scenery darkens and a spot finds the ring

skull.why: the higher the skull, the smaller, fainter and further along the light it lies

ring.why: the ring's shadow says how deep it is. Nothing joins them: no dotted line, no plumb line

landing.why: at landing the shadow and the skull meet

occlusion.why: nothing decorative covers these; the foreground frame keeps to the edges, and an element that crosses the gameplay plane must have a gameplay reason (an anchor, an obstacle)

sheet._doc: The Map Production Sheet: every map file carries one, in this order. The build refuses a map that leaves any out.

hudSafe.why: fractions of the screen the HUD owns; no gameplay object is drawn there at rest

ecosystem._doc: v58 MAP → ECOSYSTEM → CAST. Characters are not global assets: each belongs to the maps listed here and turns up nowhere else. A map's ecosystem (src/maps/*.json: ecosystem) names its cast, its wildlife, its vegetation, its props and its hazards; the build checks the cast against these rules and against what the map actually shows (its walkers, its gravedigger, its sky life, the life in its water), and runs the Map Identity Test below on every map.

identityTest.q: Would removing the background (the sky and the skyline) still leave enough environmental evidence to identify the map?
identityTest.check: at least four kinds of scenery on its track that no other map has

identityTest.q: Is every character here one that belongs here, and is anyone here who belongs nowhere else nearby?
identityTest.check: every cast member allowed on this map by the cast rules; at least one not on either neighbouring map

identityTest.q: Does something live here besides the cast?
identityTest.check: at least two kinds of wildlife, each allowed here
at least two vegetation kinds, each on its own track

identityTest.q: Could you tell it by what's lying about?
identityTest.check: at least three prop kinds, each on its own track

identityTest.q: Is the ground under Morty its own?
identityTest.check: a lane material different from both neighbours'

identityTest.q: Does the air belong to it?
Does it teach what its place in the order says it teaches?
identityTest.check: its ecosystem.teaches is the order's word for its place, and it names at least one hazard

identityTest.q: Would a swatch of its sky and its ground be mistaken for another map's?
identityTest.check: its sky and ground mid-tones at least 20 apart (RGB) from every other map's

identityTest.q: Is the end in sight, and is it its own?
identityTest.check: a lair landmark on the horizon that no other map has
